Curling from insufficient water addressed with 30-minute bottom soak and drain; central rehydration match.
Water when top two inches start drying and maintain moist soil; would lead to watering in the stated dry-soil case, though no overnight soak.

Check soil to second knuckle before watering

Alternatively stand tap water in container for two to three days
Move to humid bathroom if edges brown

resolved.reason: Moisture checks and soaking include the fix, but broad care and overwatering/cold explanation of droop obscure the dry-soil diagnosis; moisture guard prevents harmful automatic watering.

harmfulness.reason: “Always check the soil” and draining after the soak guard against waterlogging. The broad routine and twice-daily misting are unnecessary here, but no likely serious worsening follows the guarded watering advice.

specificity_accuracy.reason: The “bottom watering” method addresses the dry substrate and confirmed leaf response. However, the droop section primarily blames overwatering or cold and does not distinguish the damaged stems, so the case diagnosis is incomplete.

feasibility.reason: A finger-depth check and 10–15-minute soak are concrete. The full answer also adds location, humidity, water preparation and weekly leaf tasks, making the complete regimen much more involved than this case needs.
